title: Replace hardcoded English StateError messages in FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl with typed error codes
why: EH-5 requires domain/data errors to carry a stable code/enum, never a pre-formatted human sentence, because the app ships EN+Hebrew and a raw exception.message/.toString() renders untranslated and un-RTL-shaped. This StateError carries no `.code` field at all — contrast with the codebase's own established pattern for exactly this kind of condition: 4 presentation files (account_actions.dart, sign_in_controller.dart, signup_screen.dart, account_picker_screen.dart) all switch on `GoogleSignInException.code`, never `.message`. The one caller I traced for this specific StateError (sign_in_controller.dart `_extractFirebaseCode`) happens to fall back safely to a translated generic string because its `[plugin/code]` regex doesn't match a StateError's toString() — but that's incidental to that call site's defensive regex, not a guarantee, and the other 3 call sites (deleteAccount/changePassword/reauthenticateWithEmail flows in features/account) are outside this batch and unverified. The lint meant to catch a raw .toString() reaching UI (no_e_to_string_in_ui) is currently non-functional (custom_lint crashes — baselined), so nothing today would catch a future regression at those sites.
recommendation: Introduce a small typed exception (e.g. NotAuthenticatedException) or a stable error-code enum instead of StateError('...'); have presentation resolve display text via AppLocalizations, matching the .code-switch pattern already used for GoogleSignInException elsewhere in the codebase.
acceptance_criteria: No throw StateError('<english sentence>') remains in firebase_auth_gateway_impl.dart; a typed exception without a baked-in human sentence is thrown instead.
Existing 'throws when no user is signed in' tests updated to assert the new exception type.
A grep/test confirms no caller of deleteAccount/changePassword/reauthenticateWithEmail/sendEmailVerification renders the exception's raw message/toString() in a widget.

corrections: All 4 StateError quotes/lines (103,175,184,198) exact, and the 4-file GoogleSignInException.code-switch pattern is real. But the 'traced caller' claim is wrong: sign_in_controller.dart's resendVerificationEmail (the only caller of sendEmailVerification traced) never calls _extractFirebaseCode at all — it swallows the error into AppLogger.warning with nothing shown to the user, not a regex-fallback to generic text as narrated.
